title: Boombox Mini will not pair, fixed by the steps
setup: An anonymous visitor cannot pair their Boombox Mini with a phone. The product record has the steps: switch off and on, hold the pair button until the light blinks, delete it from the Bluetooth list and pair again, then try a second phone. The steps work.
turns: My Boombox Mini won't pair with my phone, help
Done all that and it's connected now, thanks

expected.answer: Gives the record's steps in order: switch the speaker off and on, hold the pair button until the light blinks, delete Boombox Mini from the phone's Bluetooth list and pair again. If it still fails, try a second phone, then open a support case. Does not push a repair once it works.

criteria: Uses the steps from the product record rather than generic Bluetooth advice.

title: Blip will not turn on, steps fail, in-warranty repair
setup: Ali's Blip (ORD-20127, delivered 19 Oct 2026) will not turn on. The record's steps: plug it in for 15 minutes, hold the power key for 10 seconds, try a different cable and socket. He has already tried all three. It is about a month old, so a fault is covered and the repair is free with a free label both ways.
turns: My Blip won't turn on at all. Dead.
Left it on charge 20 minutes, held the power button, tried my sister's cable. Nothing.
ORD-20127, ali.baba@example.com. Can you get it fixed?

expected.answer: Suggests the record's steps first. Once he says they failed, confirms it is inside the 24-month warranty and creates a Fix Club repair for the Blip with his description of the fault. The repair is free with a free label both ways, about 10 working days from the day it reaches the workshop.
must_not_say: a replacement is on its way

criteria: Tries the steps before raising a repair.
Repair is created once only and the fault is described in the customer's words.

ideal.fault: Will not turn on. Tried 15 minutes of charging, a 10 second power key hold and another cable.

title: Mould in the Pocket Jungle, customer wants to return it
setup: Story 28. Mowgli's Pocket Jungle (ORD-20145, delivered 14 Nov, 9 days ago, a day late on a Saturday) has mould on the soil and the leaves look unwell. CASE-9015 is open and waiting for a photo. He wants to send it back for a refund. The live plant cannot be returned for change of mind, but it has a 14-day health guarantee and he is inside it.
turns: There's mould on the soil in my Pocket Jungle and the leaves are going yellow. I want to send it back and get my money.
ORD-20145, mowgli@example.com. So can I return it or not?

expected.answer: Gives the care steps (remove the mould with the tweezers, lift the dome a few hours a day for a week, stop misting until the moss is dry, remove yellow leaves, keep it out of direct sun). Says the live plant cannot be returned for a refund but has a 14-day health guarantee and he is inside it: send a photo (CASE-9015 is waiting for one) and a new plant is arranged. Does not create a return.

criteria: Notes CASE-9015 already exists and does not open a second case.
Does not promise a replacement before a photo is seen.

title: Daypack laptop sleeve will not stay on the rails
setup: An anonymous visitor says the Daypack Laptop Sleeve keeps falling off. The record's steps: push both clips fully into slots on the same row until they click, and never load an add-on over 1.5 kg.
turns: The laptop sleeve on my Daypack keeps coming off the rails when I walk. Faulty?
It's a 16 inch laptop plus charger and a big hardback in the sleeve

expected.answer: Gives the record's steps: push both clips fully into slots on the same row until they click. Then notes an add-on must not be loaded over 1.5 kg, and a 16 inch laptop plus charger and a hardback is probably over that. If it still comes off with a light load, open a support case.

criteria: Does not declare a fault before the steps and weight limit are covered.
